 Troy Aikman would try to lure Kyle Shanahan from 49ers if running NFL team
 "First call I’d make is to the 49ers and say, ‘How much is it going to take to get Kyle Shanahan?’ Because I think he’s that good." 
 Credit: Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images 
 By Brandon Contes on 11/12/2026 11/12/2026 
 Less AI and more AA in your search results.
 If Jerry Jones hires Troy Aikman to run the Dallas Cowboys, it sounds like they will have significant philosophical differences about how and where to find a head coach.
 Aikman has long been interested in running an NFL team. But the dream has seemed more realistic in recent weeks as Aikman heads toward free agency without what he considers a serious contract offer to remain with ESPN and their Monday Night Football booth. And with his future as a broadcaster in question , Jerry Jones admitted Aikman holding a significant role with the Cowboys is “ very possible .”
 Thursday morning, Aikman joined The Musers for his weekly appearance on The Ticket in Dallas, where he fawned over Kyle Shanahan, admitting he would target the San Francisco 49ers head coach if running a team.
 “I’ve been asked a lot of questions here, certainly over the last several weeks, about any aspirations that I may have of going in a front office,” Aikman noted. “Or ‘Who would you hire as your head coach?’ If I was in a position to hire someone as a head coach, [the] first call I’d make is to the 49ers and say, ‘How much is it going to take to get Kyle Shanahan? Because I think he’s that good. And yes, I’ve always believed this, but coaching matters and it has an impact on an organization.”
 Aikman touted the 49ers as well-coached, disciplined, and physical, with their best players as tone-setters who police the locker room and hold everyone to a certain standard. And it’s not the first time Aikman has heaped praise on Shanahan. In 2022, Aikman similarly named Shanahan as the head coach he would love to hire . But in 2022, it didn’t seem plausible that Aikman would ever be in a position to poach Shanahan.
 What’s interesting about Aikman now suggesting he would be willing to give up significant assets for Shanahan is that it comes on the heels of Jerry Jones claiming there’s no correlation between paying a head coach and winning . In recent weeks, Aikman and Jones have expressed mutual interest in working together with the Cowboys, but questions remain about whether they could work together. They’re not working together yet, but it sounds like there are already major philosophical differences about how to hire a head coach.
